classification.difficultyReason: Use equal-edge marks and the common prism length to infer equal rectangular face areas, then count two triangular ends and three rectangles.

content.prompt: Calculate the surface area of these triangular prisms.

spec.description: Obliquely oriented triangular prism with an unshaded rectangular face and triangular end. All three edges of the triangular end carry matching single ticks. Only source-visible edges are drawn.
spec.mathematics: The triangular end has area 76 mm². The adjacent rectangular face has area 82 mm². Equal triangular-end edges imply three equal rectangular face areas.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied face areas are visible; the total surface area is withheld.

answer.worked:
The equal-edge marks show that all three rectangular faces have the same area.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total surface area}&=2\times76+3\times82\\&=398\ \mathrm{mm}^{2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangular prism with an unshaded front triangular end and right rectangular face. All three front-triangle edges carry matching single ticks. Only source-visible edges are drawn.
spec.mathematics: The triangular end has area 24 cm². The adjacent rectangular face has area 44 cm². Equal triangular-end edges imply three equal rectangular face areas.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied face areas are visible; the total surface area is withheld.

answer.worked:
The equal-edge marks show that all three rectangular faces have the same area.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total surface area}&=2\times24+3\times44\\&=180\ \mathrm{cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$
